name: Generating Assessments
title: Generating Assessments
answer: Generating assessments in course design and teaching means using AI to produce quiz items, exam questions, rubrics, practice problems, and feedback prompts from learning objectives and course materials. It covers item types such as multiple choice, short answer, essay prompts, and performance tasks, along with answer keys and scoring guides. The work sits between instructional design, subject matter expertise, and assessment theory, so it is not just text generation. It also includes aligning items to outcomes, difficulty, and cognitive level.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Generating assessments in course design and teaching means using AI to produce quiz items, exam questions, rubrics, practice problems, and feedback prompts from learning objectives and course materials. It covers item types such as multiple choice, short answer, essay prompts, and performance tasks, along with answer keys and scoring guides. The work sits between instructional design, subject matter expertise, and assessment theory, so it is not just text generation. It also includes aligning items to outcomes, difficulty, and cognitive level.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: What it runs on includes learning management systems, item banks, and authoring tools, plus large language models or specialized question generation models. Course materials, textbooks, lecture notes, and existing question banks are common inputs. Retrieval layers and vector stores help ground generation in approved content. Outputs may be stored in QTI or similar formats for LMS import, with version control and review queues.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: How the work is done starts with a blueprint that maps objectives to item types and coverage. Then a practitioner prompts or fine-tunes a model with source passages, examples, and constraints, and generates candidate items. Subject experts review for accuracy, clarity, bias, and alignment, then edit and pilot. Statistical checks like item difficulty and discrimination follow after student responses. The site's 12,646 extracted claims can support tracing a factual statement back to a research source.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk and provenance: generated items may reproduce copyrighted text or leak sensitive data from prompts. Provenance matters, so keep records of source materials, model versions, prompts, and human edits. Risks include biased or culturally narrow examples, ambiguous wording, answer key errors, and accessibility barriers. Academic integrity and privacy rules apply when using student data or deploying assessments. Human review remains the control point for high stakes exams.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Where it is going: more automated item generation tied to psychometric models, adaptive testing, and multimodal items that include images, code, or simulations. Expect tighter integration with LMS analytics and learning objectives, plus better provenance and audit trails. Open questions include fairness, validity, and how to credit human and machine contributions. The field is moving toward human in the loop workflows rather than full automation.
